business_problem: E.ON provides energy networks and infrastructure for 48 million customers across Europe. Helping power a continent is a big responsibility, and the company needs up-to-the-minute data to continue making the strategic decisions that keep the business at the forefront of the industry.
solution_summary: E.ON provides energy networks and infrastructure for 48 million customers across Europe. Helping power a continent is a big responsibility, and the company needs up-to-the-minute data to continue making the strategic decisions that keep the business at the forefront of the industry. As of the second half of 2023, nearly 12,000 enthusiastic E.ON employees use Power BI to propel decision-making, ushering in a new era of data democratization throughout E.ON. E.ON used Power BI, Microsoft Teams, Microsoft 365 to support real-time analytics with a governed operating model that connected the relevant data sources, automation logic, and employee-facing experiences without custom point-to-point tooling.

Granted to whichever company currently has the most customers in a region, this status makes the base supplier the default energy supplier for any new customer in the region.
“Power BI had a clear advantage over other tools in terms of interoperability with the Microsoft 365 platform. We face no obstacles in getting data to the right place.”

When he began his current role, Jan Finke, IT Service Owner, Business Intelligence and Visualization Technologies at E.ON Digital Technology GmbH, was tasked with advancing and scaling E.ON’s existing internal Power BI platform service. According to Finke, Power BI stood out as a great fit for a large, multifaceted company like E.ON and has since become the most in-demand data visualization product compared to the company’s alternative solutions.
